support_cases.title: Decision: Kestrel retries a failed job five times

expectations: If a memory states that Kestrel retries a failed job three times, it is judged unsupported.
If a memory states that Kestrel waits 10, 60 and 300 seconds between retries, it is judged unsupported.
If a memory states that a fixed retry schedule was chosen over exponential backoff, it is judged unsupported.
If a memory states that a job whose last retry fails moves to the kestrel-dlq queue, and states nothing about how many times or how long Kestrel retries, it is judged supported.
Every memory judged unsupported states the count of three retries, the waits of 10, 60 and 300 seconds, or the choice of a fixed schedule over exponential backoff.

support_cases.title: Incident review: the Kestrel queue stalled on 2026-09-12

expectations: If a memory states that the on-call engineer is paged when no job has started for five minutes, it is judged unsupported.
If a memory states that a startup check refuses to run the queue with fsync off, and states nothing about paging, it is judged supported.
Every memory judged unsupported states that the on-call engineer is paged when no job has started.

support_cases.title: Runbook: rotating the Kestrel signing key

expectations: If a memory states that a rotation waits until every worker reports the new key id in `kestrel-admin status`, it is judged supported.
No memory is judged unsupported.

support_cases.title: 决定：Kestrel 的失败告警只发到 #kestrel-oncall

expectations: If a memory states that the on-call engineer must acknowledge an alert within 15 minutes, it is judged unsupported.
If a memory states that Kestrel's failure alerts go only to the Slack channel #kestrel-oncall, and states no time to acknowledge them, it is judged supported.
Every memory judged unsupported states the 15-minute time to acknowledge an alert.
If a memory states that the backup job copies the queue database every 6 hours, it is judged unsupported.
If a memory states that each copy is kept for 30 days in the bucket kestrel-archive, and states nothing about how often a copy is made, it is judged supported.
Every memory judged unsupported states that a copy is made every 6 hours.
If a memory states that a job payload may be at most 256 KiB, it is judged unsupported.
If a memory states that each tenant may have at most 500 jobs in flight, and states no payload limit, it is judged supported.
Every memory judged unsupported states the 256 KiB payload limit.
If a memory states that a page must be acknowledged within 5 minutes, it is judged unsupported.
If a memory states that a page the primary does not acknowledge escalates to the secondary on-call engineer, and states no 5-minute limit, it is judged supported.
Every memory judged unsupported states the 5-minute time to acknowledge a page.

support_cases.title: KES-42: Webhook delivery timeout is too short for slow receivers

expectations: If a memory states the decision to raise the webhook delivery timeout to 20 seconds, it is judged unsupported.
If a memory states that timed-out deliveries are logged to the kestrel-webhook-audit stream, it is judged unsupported.
Every memory judged unsupported states the 20-second timeout, the kestrel-webhook-audit stream, or that deliveries time out after 5 seconds.
If a memory states that the invoices queue waits at most 2 minutes, it is judged unsupported.
Every memory judged unsupported states the 2-minute maximum wait of the invoices queue.
If a memory states that the status page keeps the 99.9% availability panel, it is judged unsupported.
Every memory judged unsupported states the 99.9% availability panel.
If a memory states that the canary covers 5% of tenants, it is judged unsupported.
If a memory states that Kestrel 4.2 ships behind the kestrel-canary flag, and states no share of tenants, it is judged supported.
Every memory judged unsupported states that the canary covers 5% of tenants.
